newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt looks to speed up flood relief bonds.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt looks to speed up flood relief bonds.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday asked the Finance Ministry to speed up a bond issue to pay for flood relief, as the country continues to mop up from one of its worst disasters in a century.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told journalists after a weekly government meeting that he hoped a second one billion crown ($28.6 million) tranche of five-year bonds would be hastened in order to help limit economic damage from the flooding.

"It's possible that the issue (originally planned to be launched on September 1) may occur a few days earlier," he said, adding that some 2,300 people in the area, which has the country's highest unemployment rate, had been put to work in the clean-up operation.
Apart from the flood bonds, the government has pledged some five billion crowns in privatisation proceeds and is considering a loan of more than 10 billion crowns from the European Investment Bank.

Klaus added on Wednesday that he expects the government to announce further support measures for firms affected by the flooding next week, but that it was most likely the help would come in the form of indirect, and not direct, aid.
"We will consider the possible choices for indirect help such as delaying debt payments," he said.
Severe flooding caused by torrential rains last month devastated parts of the east of the Czech Republic, as well as parts of western Poland, killing some 100 people.
Officials say Czech river levels have since receded, with most areas now out of danger.
As people return to their homes, damage estimates continue to grow. Economists have put the cost at 50-100 billion crowns.

The first tranche of bonds was issued with a fixed rate of 12.5 percent for the first year. The final four years of maturity would have an interest rate equal to the average inflation rate for the previous 12 months plus 250 basis points.

Finance Minister Ivan Pilip has said the second tranche will be issued with the same conditions. The first two tranches are mainly intended for retail investors, but Pilip said a third tranche for larger institutions was being considered.

He added that the timing of the issue for institutional investors should be announced by the beginning of September and that further details should be available within the next week. ($ = 34.90 Czech Crowns)
